title: Incremental contemporaneous movement information in motor gamma

titles: AJILE12 naturalistic human movement and ECoG

scientific_question: Does prespecified motor-channel 80–100 Hz log power improve same-window wrist-speed prediction over behavior state and time of day in held-out patients or, separately, held-out days of the same patient?
primary_outputs: Independently computed paired difference in held-out movement MSE between state/time baseline and gamma-augmented prediction; positive, null and negative increments are all valid. Matched high-minus-low movement gamma contrasts are secondary.

inputs: Bounded exported ECoG samples×channels, actual ecog_time_s and validity mask; anatomy-selected motor channels fixed before outcomes.
Selected contralateral wrist xy pose, actual pose times, confidence and validity for operator target construction; exact behavior state epochs and qualified local time offset.
Gamma feature: demean each independent 2-second window, Hann taper, integrate one-sided periodogram for 80≤f<100 Hz, then mean natural-log power over fixed motor channels.

primary.name: Equal-patient, equal-day held-out baseline-minus-gamma movement MSE, pixels²/second²
primary.aggregation: MSE within each patient/day, equal mean across days within patient, then equal mean across patients. State the split mode.
primary.rationale: Reports the signed fixed-comparator prediction increment on all supported days, including constant-target days. Positive, null and negative increments are valid scientific answers. A larger increment is not an unrestricted contestant reward or evidence of better interpretation; the existing evaluator computes the contrast but supplies no answer-error rubric for an investigator report.

secondary: Delta R² with its defined-day/patient counts; constant-target days remain undefined for R² but retain MSE.
Matched high-minus-low gamma log-power differences, matched/unmatched coverage and patient/day summaries.
Complete baseline/gamma/day-shift predictions, per-day errors and exclusion ledger; source pixels remain explicit.

comparators.name: State/time ridge baseline
comparators.inputs: State one-hot terms and daily sine/cosine phase.
comparators.procedure: Fixed alpha=1 weighted ridge with unpenalized intercept; training weights equal patients, days within patient and windows within day; train-only scaling.

comparators.name: Matched gamma-augmented ridge
comparators.inputs: Exactly the baseline design plus fixed motor gamma log-power feature.
comparators.procedure: Same alpha, train-only scaling and held-out rows; nuisance-feature shrinkage can still affect conditional interpretation, so this fixed-estimator increment is not all possible neural information.

comparators.name: Prespecified matched windows and temporal diagnostic
comparators.inputs: Held-out windows matched within patient/day/exact state/hour; gamma circularly shifted by half the ordered day sequence for a separate diagnostic.
comparators.procedure: High/low threshold is training-window median speed; greedily match nearest unused opposite-group window within 300 seconds. Refit shifted model; gaps/state changes and wrap prevent exchangeable-null claims.

evaluation.uncertainty: Descriptive 2,000-draw seed-50 patient cluster bootstrap of patient summaries, with day averaging before resampling. No interval for fewer than two contributing patients; endpoint-specific support counts must accompany intervals. Overlapping train folds and limited cohort constrain generalization.
evaluation.failure_policy: Reject invalid manifests/clocks/source IDs, cross-session interval overlaps, split-guard violations, unsupported training states and nonfinite predictions. Retain excluded windows and reasons; require complete target IDs for both predictors. Undefined R² is reported with counts, never used to replace full-support MSE.
